subject: Re: Pricing alignment request — Hosted API commit tiers & match to OpenAI
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@finova.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@finova.com
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing — request to align with OpenAI offer

Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and the rollout controls look promising. Procurement flagged that our existing vendor (OpenAI) has provided a near-term promotional rate for our projected consumption, and finance asked whether Redwood can match or come close on per-token rates if we commit.

Specifically they're asking for: 40B input+output tokens/month equivalent for 12 months with a blended per-token price that is ~25% below your public list. They want to understand how commit tiers and burst/baseline capacity would work (we need predictable latency for customer-facing flows).

Can you send a clear map of commit tiers, the associated per-token prices, and any guardrails (min monthly invoice, early-termination, overage pricing)? Also, if you can provide a direct comparison to the OpenAI endpoint price given in the attached spreadsheet, that would be very helpful.

Best,
Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Product
Finova

Attachment: Finova_COMPARISON.xlsx (spreadsheet with competitor quote pasted)

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@finova.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 13:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing — request to align with OpenAI offer

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. I pulled together a concise proposal attached (PDF) and a quick summary below. Short answer: we can get very close to the blended per-token economics if you take a 12-month commit with a predictable baseline and a capped burst window.

Summary (high level):
- Baseline commit: 40B tokens/month, 12-month term.
- Blended per-token: $0.00012 per token (input+output combined) at that commit level — this is a 22% effective discount vs our public price.
- Burst: additional headroom up to 1.75x baseline at a higher incremental rate ($0.00016/token) to preserve SLOs.
- Min monthly invoice: 90% of the committed spend (standard for reserved capacity).
- Early termination: pro-rated repayment of the committed discount differential over remaining months.
- SLA and latency: we will allocate Dedicated-backed routing with reserved GPUs to keep 95th percentile latency within the SLA you saw in the demo.

I've attached Redwood_HostedAPI_Commit_Tiers_v2.pdf with tier table, example math, and proposed signature page. If you want, we can structure it as a two-line quote (Reserved commit + usage overage) or as a fully blended monthly invoice.

I'll loop in pricing and legal if you signal interest. Quick question: does finance need an explicit 'match to OpenAI' clause, or is an equivalently priced committed quote acceptable?

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_HostedAPI_Commit_Tiers_v2.pdf

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@finova.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@finova.com
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing — request to align with OpenAI offer

Ben — appreciate the fast turnaround. Finance specifically asked that any match be explicit against the OpenAI line-item they provided; they want written confirmation that if OpenAI honors the published promotional band for the first 6 months we would get a corresponding adjustment or credit. They also want clarity on what model variants are included (we use both standard completion and a higher-cost instruction/chat variant).

Two follow-ups: can you confirm whether the 22% discount applies to both model variants? And can you provide sample invoice math (monthly invoice row-by-row) so our billing team can reconcile?

Alex

Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pricing — request to align with OpenAI offer

Team — looping you in. Finova is asking for a written match to an OpenAI promotional band for a 12-month, 40B tok/mo commit. Key constraints: must cover both standard generation and the chat/instruction variant they use; they require predictable 95th percentile latency for customer flows.

Proposed conservative commercial structure:
- 12mo commit: 40B tok/mo baseline
- Effective blended rate: $0.000125/token for baseline (we absorb a portion of cost through optimized quantization profiles & batching)
- Burst pricing up to 1.75x baseline at $0.00017/token
- Explicit competitor-match clause: provide a retroactive credit for any verified competitor promotional delta for first 6 months, capped at 10% of committed ARR. That gives them an assurance while limiting Redwood downside.

Questions for legal/pricing: is the retroactive credit cap reasonable? Also need confirmation that Dedicated-backed routing covering the commit will include agreed quantization/optimization profiles (we may need to lock model variants to ensure parity).

Thanks — Ben

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@finova.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing — request to align with OpenAI offer

Ben / team — thanks for the thoughtful carve. A few redlines from pricing/legal perspective:
1) The retroactive credit is acceptable in principle, but not open-ended. Cap at 10% of committed ARR is reasonable; add a verification process (they must furnish the competitor invoice/contract).
2) For model variants: we should enumerate 'base' and 'chat/instruction' buckets. The discount will apply to both buckets but at slightly different rates — chat variant +8% uplift vs base due to higher footprint. We can provide sample invoice rows (line items: baseline tokens @ blended rate, burst tokens @ incremental, chat variant uplift).
3) Min invoice floor: prefer 95% rather than 90% to reduce churn risk.

I'll prep a short memo and sample invoice rows; PrIyom, can you please draft the two-line quote + sample monthly invoice rows and attach to the PDF? Marissa — can you sign off on the verification language for the competitor-match clause?

Laura
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 16:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing — request to align with OpenAI offer

Agree with Laura's edits. A couple of practical notes before we send to Finova:
- Verification: require the competitor promo to be documented (signed quote or procurement email) and timebound to the first 6 months; our retro credit will be applied as a single invoice credit in month 7.
- Model parity: lock to the agreed model versions (we'll list them in the SOW) and include a small clause allowing us to propose a migration path if the upstream model changes materially.
- Invoice floor: 95% is fine. Let's keep burst capped at 1.5x instead of 1.75x to be conservative on capacity.

Ben — please send the updated two-line quote, include the sample monthly invoice rows in the PDF, and add the verification language. Alex — if this structure sounds acceptable I can approve the retro credit cap and we can move to signature.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
